notes.text: Jonathan Marchessault is day to day (lower-body injury) and has missed the last 2 games. He is a top-six forward.
Daemon Hunt joined from MIN on Oct 25 and has played beside Jayden Struble.
Shane Wright joined from SEA on Nov 2 and has played beside Filip Forsberg and Nils Höglander.
Adam Edström has started killing penalties: on the ice for 33% of the team’s shorthanded time in 16 games, up from 1% with his old team last season.

The forward lines keep changing. Even their four most-used trios over the last 10 games cover only 31% of their forwards’ 5-on-5 time, the 8th-lowest in the league (a typical team: 39%). The lines listed lean on their latest games, but expect new combinations tonight.
Troy Terry is on long-term injured reserve (hip surgery) and has missed the last 8 games. He is one of their most valuable skaters.
A.J. Greer is on injured reserve (upper body injury) and has missed the last 3 games. He is one of their more valuable skaters. Nico Myatovic has taken his spot beside Sam Colangelo and Tim Washe.

story.head: The Ducks are on a heater
paras: The Ducks have won four straight, and the Predators have won three straight. The Predators played last night, and the Ducks are rested. Going in, the Predators are fifth in the Central (tied for 14th in the NHL) and the Ducks fourth in the Pacific (tied for 14th).

The Predators’ record (.594) is running ahead of what their chances are worth (.525), largely thanks to pulling off wins in one-goal games. So is the Ducks’ (.559 on chances worth .485), largely thanks to their finishing.

The Predators keep things calm after the whistle (3rd lowest), get pinned in their own end on long shifts (32nd) and give up a lot of shots (31st). On the other side, the Ducks are one of the league’s most physical teams (2nd), have had shaky goaltending (30th) and give up a lot of dangerous shots (30th). Anaheim has scored 3.76 goals a game, the fourth most in the league, and allowed 3.76, the third most. Both teams like to play fast, so expect an open game. On top of that, the Ducks hound the puck, but the Preds sit back.

Filip Forsberg (5 G / 14 A / 19 P in 16 GP) leads the Predators in scoring, with eight points in his last five games and six goals in nine games against Anaheim since 2023-24. Steven Stamkos (9 G / 8 A / 17 P in 16 GP) has a team-high nine goals. Leo Carlsson (6 G / 20 A / 26 P in 17 GP) leads the Ducks in scoring and is tied for sixth in the NHL, with eleven points in his last five games. Cutter Gauthier (12 G / 6 A / 18 P in 16 GP) has a team-high twelve goals, tied for fourth in the NHL, with eleven points in his last five games.

Justus Annunen (3-1-0 / .873 SV% in 4 GS) will likely start for Nashville. Anaheim has two options in net: Lukáš Dostál (4-4-1 / .866 SV% in 10 GS) and Laurent Brossoit (3-0-0 / .847 SV% in 3 GS). Dostál has started four of their last ten games, including the last one on Friday. It’s anyone’s guess who gets the net.

The Ducks are newly without A.J. Greer, and have been without Troy Terry and Tyson Hinds for several games. Taking into account how much value each of these missing players usually adds, only the Mammoth are missing more right now.
Filip Forsberg has a point in four straight games against Anaheim, with a goal in each of the last three.
Cutter Gauthier has twelve goals on chances worth about 6.6 goals, well above what his finishing usually turns chances into. Runs like that tend to cool off.
